title: Prime Books Primary Standard, Years 1 to 4
revision_note: A-2.2 supersedes A-2.1: the teacher delegated the five open items, added the Welcome cast, the QR policy, the References section, the safe-margin rule and the image-reference workflow.

scope.collection: Standard A (Primary). Standard B, Years 7 to 12, is not touched by this lock.
scope.unit_page_reference: y01 Physical Education, Unit 1 'Moving well', physical page 12
scope.contents_component_reference: y01 Physical Education master contents page (bar plus one card per unit)
scope.print_route: BookVault, perfect-bound paperback. No other printer is planned, so printing constrains the page.

geometry.unit: millimetres are the source of truth for print, points for authoring, converted at 72/25.4
geometry.margin_note: mirrored margins: the inner margin is deeper than the outer one, because BookVault binds on the inner edge
geometry.safe_area_note: 20 mm (56.7 pt) from the binding edge, 5 mm (14.2 pt) from the other three trim edges

extent.rule: interior page count is one less than a multiple of 12: 11, 23, 35, 47, 59, 71, 83, 95, 107, 119, 131 ...
extent.applies_to: the interior file, after the front and back covers are stripped for the cover wrap
extent.formula: round UP to the next legal count; never round down, never pad with a blank page
extent.budget: front matter 7 pages + units + back matter 12 to 14 pages (glossary, references, sources, closing), then round up to the nearest 12n-1
extent.blank_page_note: a page that exists is a page that teaches, gives workspace or records sources. Padding to reach a legal count is done with usable content, never with white space.
extent.reserves_last_page: BookVault prints its production barcode on the last interior page: keep that page clear in its lower area

unit_page_header.rule: the unit name appears ONCE at the top of a unit page
unit_page_header.on_the_opener: unit eyebrow, numeral, unit title, subtitle. No running head repeating the unit name above or below it
unit_page_header.on_topic_pages: the running head in the 47 pt band carries 'Unit n, Unit name' and the kicker carries 'UNIT n, TOPIC x.y' with the topic title. Do not print the unit name a third time in the body
unit_page_header.reason: measured on the y01 PE Unit 1 opener: the unit name was repeated, and the tracked eyebrow started at x 36.8 pt, which is 13 mm from the trim, 7 mm inside BookVault's 20 mm gutter
unit_page_header.enforced: every piece of furniture sits inside safe_area_pt

year_ladder.basis: adopted defaults for Years 1 to 4, advisory while a book is being authored, re-measured after the first Year 1 book is rebuilt

unit_palette.rule: unit n takes rung n in every book of the series, so the same unit number is the same colour in every subject

rungs.name: ochre
rungs.basis: locked 14 September 2026, mid set to the house ochre for 4.73:1 on a white numeral

page_map.note: no folio, full-bleed art, year stripe on the spine edge
publisher identity, year, tagline, INSIDE THIS BOOK, IMPRINT rows, AI disclosure when generated art is used
colour bar with one segment per unit, then one card per unit
invitation plus THIS SUBJECT'S OWN CAST: the characters that will appear through the book, named, with the subject's own wardrobe
labels, icons and meanings defined once, including how to use a QR code in class
each unit: opener, get started, concept and model, your turn, extension, applied project, reflection, word bank
demonstrate the learning, not an exhibition
two columns of cards: image, headword, short definition
every information source used in the book: books, websites, datasets, image credits and licences, one per row, with the page or topic it supports
the printed list of every QR target, so a teacher can read the addresses without a phone
kept clear for BookVault's printed barcode
printed again in the cover wrap, so it is stripped from the interior file

contents_component.form: one colour bar segment per unit, then one tinted card per unit
contents_component.segment_count: equals the number of units, never fixed at six
card_rows: Unit n, How did it go?
contents_component.front_and_back_matter: plain dot-leader rows, including the glossary and the references section
contents_component.page_numbers: generated from the built PDF and verified against the real page index

welcome_cast.rule: every subject has its OWN cast, named and dressed for that subject. No shared six across the year group
welcome_cast.count: 4 to 6 named characters, chosen for the subject
welcome_cast.on_page: portrait, name and one short line of character, in the welcome grid; the same characters then carry the narrative scenes through the whole book
welcome_cast.consistency: locked by an image reference, not by memory
welcome_cast.reference_route: google/gemini-3-pro-image through the OpenRouter chat endpoint with the approved character sheet as the image reference; this is the only route that actually holds the character, because openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst ignores a reference image
welcome_cast.cost_note: scene generation stays on openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst at quality medium; the reference route is used only when an existing character must appear

qr_policy.purpose: a teacher standing in front of the class can show the activity on the board in one scan
qr_policy.placement: at the point of the activity, inside the topic page, next to the instruction it belongs to. Not collected on a single page at the back
qr_policy.frequency: roughly one per unit of 8 to 14 pages, more in practical subjects, none where there is nothing worth showing
qr_policy.size: minimum 74 x 74 pt on a white card, 4 pt inset, quiet zone respected
qr_policy.caption: every code is captioned with what it shows and how long it runs, in the child's reading size
qr_policy.verification: every URL is fetched and every code is decoded back out of the rendered page before the book is published
qr_policy.print_list: every target is also printed as a readable address in the back matter, so the book survives a dead link
qr_policy.screen: the flipbook shows the same link as text next to the code

illustration.direction: original Beatrix Potter style: fine ink contours, transparent watercolour, warm muted pigments, lightly textured cream paper

generation.reference_field: an image_url content part on the chat completions endpoint
generation.note: medium quality is the house setting: it renders plate lettering correctly and keeps the cost per page sane

grade.1-2: large actions, short sequences, direct naming, generous response space
grade.3-4: more process detail, comparisons, labelled evidence, less decorative cast

print.colour: CMYK converted once through one FOGRA profile; body and heading black is 100 percent K, never a rich black
print.transparency: flattened, so character art is composited rather than left on alpha
print.images: 300 dpi target, 150 dpi absolute floor, native pixels recorded
print.cover_wrap_formula: 2 x trim width + spine + 3 mm + 3 mm, by trim height + 3 mm + 3 mm
print.spine: BookVault's sizing calculator figure for the stock actually ordered, rounded up to a whole millimetre. The 0.056 mm per page in their worked example is a bond-paper figure: measure the first proof with calipers and correct spine_per_page_mm if it is out by more than 0.5 mm. Spine text only from 6 mm, centred and K only

decided_2026_09_14: palette rungs 5 and 6 locked: sage #2F5233 / #4E7C52 / #E8F0E3 and ochre #6B4A0C / #9A6A12 / #FBF0D8, chosen so a white folio numeral keeps 4.7:1 or better
authoring size stays US Letter 612 x 792 pt; the 216 x 279 mm print trim is the same physical book within 0.4 mm, and the pack builder normalises. No corpus migration
extent is a formula, not a fixed budget: round up to the next 12n-1, with unit page budgets of 8 to 10 at Year 1 rising to 12 to 14 at Year 4, and no blank pages
the spine figure is a measured number, not an assumed one: use the calculator, then confirm with calipers on the first physical proof
year ladder, handwriting ruling and words per page are locked as advisory authoring numbers and re-measured after the first Year 1 rebuild
open_items: the real spine width from BookVault's sizing calculator for the stock actually ordered
